### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via RuntimeConfigPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8408d82263f2c555305425f7e9d581151469d73` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1aa289a822ec91ecf662f84dbb83c1cd4beb2456` — the merge of head `66f365013a1c054e71b71993cfa0baf134b09385` into base `b8408d82263f2c555305425f7e9d581151469d73`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1aa289a822ec91ecf662f84dbb83c1cd4beb2456 && git checkout 1aa289a822ec91ecf662f84dbb83c1cd4beb2456
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b8408d82263f2c555305425f7e9d581151469d73 66f365013a1c054e71b71993cfa0baf134b09385 && git checkout -B drift-repro b8408d82263f2c555305425f7e9d581151469d73 && git merge --no-ff 66f365013a1c054e71b71993cfa0baf134b09385

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8408d82263f2c555305425f7e9d581151469d73
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b8408d82263f2c555305425f7e9d581151469d73` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T18:01Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `66f365013a1c054e71b71993cfa0baf134b09385`

Read against claim 6953457788 on #34622 (restated, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`) and amendment 6955910260 (the cloud-connection README row).
- **Size:** merge base `d576509c`, 9 files, +406/-7.
- **Not governed:** `check-governed-merges --branch pr-34945` reports 0 of 9 paths on the register and 413 lines.
- **CI at this head:** 52 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Claim surface:** all 9 files are inside the claim as amended.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** `Part of #34622` is right. This is the `cloudHomeUrl` slice only. Item 4 (#34591) and the other `cloudConsoleUrl()` callers are named as out of scope.
- **Producer (`runtime-config-plugin.ts`).** It follows the `upgradeUrl` contract line for line:
  - empty or whitespace reads as unset;
  - the existing `isAbsoluteHttpUrl` gates acceptance;
  - a refused spelling is kept and named once in `start()`;
  - the served value is a conditional spread, so an absent key never reaches the payload as `undefined`.
  - It is a host option only, with no env var, and the docblock says so.
- **Reader (`runtime-config.ts`).** It reads the top-level key the same way `upgradeUrl` is read: verbatim, with absent, empty and non-string all leaving it absent, and re-derived from each payload so a later payload withdraws it. `getCloudHomeUrl()` composes nothing from `getCloudBase()`.
- **Page.** `getCloudHomeUrl() ?? cloudConsoleUrl()` keeps today's target and show/hide rule byte for byte when the key is absent. The one behaviour change (the link is drawn on an empty `cloudUrl` when the key is declared) is stated under Acceptance notes and pinned.
- **Pins.**
  - Server: declared verbatim beside `cloudUrl`/`upgradeUrl` with no warning; no normalisation; absent; empty and whitespace silent; five refused spellings, each named in the warning; a refused value leaves `upgradeUrl` alone.
  - Console reader: 8 tests, including withdrawal on a later payload and a nested `features.cloudHomeUrl` that is not read.
  - Page: 4 cases, two declared and two CONTROL, with the real `cloudConsoleUrl`.
- **Ablations.** Both legs went red in the expected direction (server 2 red, console 4 red), the CONTROL pins stayed green, and the restores were checked by blob.
- **Changesets.** There is one patch changeset per package. Each says `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the claim, and its text matches the diff.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: The Console takes `cloudHomeUrl` verbatim with no scheme check and relies on the producer's refusal. This matches the `upgradeUrl` reader, so it is consistent, not a defect. A Console-side http(s) guard on both keys would be a separate card if anyone wants defence in depth.
- N2: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was not measured locally (no full build). CI is green on this head, so that covers it.
- N3: The cloud-repo declaration of `cloudHomeUrl` is named in the body as a follow-up and not filed, per the seat's 16:04Z ruling. Until it lands, the link keeps opening the Cloud origin.

Landing: not governed and green on this exact head. Because of `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, it goes to the seat's L2 before area o3-H lands it. A later push owes a delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `66f365013a1c054e71b71993cfa0baf134b09385`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #34622, its body and all 9 comments (triage 6937603697, premise correction 6947939206, claim 6949560908, slice-1 report 6951029706, amendment 6951594578, part-landed 6953400966, restated claim 6953457788, slice-2 report 6955880029, amendment 6955910260); the body, file list (9 files, +406 −7) and net diff of PR #34945 at the head; the 62 check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff (`isAbsoluteHttpUrl`, the `upgradeUrl` producer and reader, the app-shell barrel, the ETag helper) was read at the head and not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff implies four public-surface changes. It changes no accept set that a metadata author writes to.

1. **`RuntimeConfigPluginConfig.cloudHomeUrl?: string`** (`@objectstack/cloud-connection`, exported config type). **Right.** The option is new and optional, so no existing host option changes meaning. The constructor's three lines repeat the `upgradeUrl` block step for step. A value that is empty or only whitespace reads as unset. The check is the same module-private `isAbsoluteHttpUrl`: a WHATWG parse with no base, and only `http:`/`https:` accepted. An accepted value is kept verbatim. A refused value is kept so it can be named once in a `warn` at `start()`, in the same shape as the `upgradeUrl` refusal. It is a host option only, with no env var, which also matches `upgradeUrl`. So the validation matches `upgradeUrl` exactly.
2. **`GET /api/v1/runtime/config` gains an optional top-level `cloudHomeUrl`.** **Right, and backward compatible.**
   - It goes through the same conditional spread as `upgradeUrl`, so an undeclared or refused value serves no key at all, never `''` and never a present-but-undefined property.
   - No existing key moves or changes. `cloudUrl`, `upgradeUrl`, `features` and `branding` are pinned unchanged beside it, and the refused case pins `upgradeUrl`, `cloudUrl` and `features.aiStudio` intact.
   - Old consoles ignore the key. The console's `initRuntimeConfig` picks named fields one by one and never spreads the body, so an older bundle drops the key.
   - The ETag hashes the bytes sent (`representation-validator.ts`), so caches revalidate when a host starts declaring it.
3. **app-shell: `AppShellRuntimeConfig.cloudHomeUrl?` and the new export `getCloudHomeUrl()`** from `runtime-config.ts`. Like `getUpgradeUrl`, it is not added to the package barrel. **Right.**
   - The reader is the line-for-line twin of the `upgradeUrl` reader from #34879. A non-empty string is taken verbatim. Absent, empty, whitespace, non-string and nested-under-`features` values all stay absent. Each payload re-derives the key, so a later payload without it withdraws it. All of these cases are pinned.
   - The getter never composes a value from `getCloudBase`.
4. **The marketplace install dialog's "Open on Cloud" link** now opens `getCloudHomeUrl() ?? cloudConsoleUrl()`. **Right.**
   - The reader never yields `''`, so `??` falls back exactly when the key is absent.
   - With the key absent, the target and the show/hide rule are byte-identical to before: the link opens the origin, and it is not drawn when `cloudConsoleUrl()` is `''`. Both cases are pinned as CONTROL cases, using the real `cloudConsoleUrl`.
   - `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"` is kept and pinned.
   - The one new behaviour, a link drawn when the key is declared on an empty `cloudUrl`, is declared in the acceptance notes and pinned. It matches ruling cloud#1850 A ("render the link when present"). This is the same shape the merged `upgradeUrl` slice took.

**Validation is pinned.** Five refused values are each pinned as served-absent and named in the mount warning: `/_console`, `_console/`, the bare host `cloud.example.com/_console`, `javascript:alert(1)` and `ftp://…`. The empty and whitespace values are pinned as absent and silent. "Verbatim" (case, port, query, fragment, trailing slash) is pinned on both the server and the console. Both ablations in the PR body went red in the expected direction and were restored to HEAD.

**The runtime-only ruling holds.**
- No path under `packages/spec` is in the diff. The runtime-config payload has no `packages/spec` declaration: neither `upgradeUrl` nor `mapStyleUrl` appears there, and the spec's `RuntimeConfig` hits are the unrelated sandbox type.
- The key is a TypeScript host option, which a metadata author cannot write. So `Metadata-protocol: none` is the correct kind.
- The triage asked for the key to be named on the card before claiming. The restated claim 6953457788 names it as `cloudHomeUrl`, with its contract, for cloud#4792 / PR #4804 to consume.

**Part of, not Closes.** The PR body says `Part of #34622`, which is correct: item 4 (#34591) stays open on the card.

**Gates.** All 62 check-runs on the head are `completed`, with 0 failures. 52 succeeded, including Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check UI, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (10/10 shards), Test UI and its planned shards, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI and Dogfood Regression Gate. 10 were skipped: the opt-in, queue-only and schedule jobs. The head has no legacy commit statuses. The dev's locally NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` belongs to the CI lint families, which concluded green.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/34622-cloud-home-url-server.md`: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch`.
- `.changeset/34622-cloud-home-url-console.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

Each changeset body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations. They are identical to the PR body's two lines and to the restated claim 6953457788. **The level is right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 says the level follows the kind alone, and `none` takes `patch`. A non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The diff publishes no breaking change: there is no removal or rename, so no migration and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. Both packages the diff moves have an entry, and app-shell changesets are established repo practice even though the package is `private`. Check Changeset is green.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — correct. It adds a new optional key to a served payload, a new optional host option, a new optional field on an exported console config type and a new console getter. Every addition is absent by default, and no existing key, option, default or meaning changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Slice-2 dev flags.** The report 6955880029 has `open_questions: []` and `security_findings: none`. Its one out-of-scope finding is the cloud distribution declaring `cloudHomeUrl`, with carrier cloud, noted and not filed. It is named in the PR body as the cloud-repo follow-up, and the restated claim puts it out of scope. **Answered:** until cloud declares the key, the link keeps today's origin target, so nothing regresses here.
- **Slice-1 open question (report 6951029706), carried on this card. Answered.**
  - (1) Test layout. The claim amendment 6951594578 settled it on AGENTS.md's shared-harness rule (ruling record 6583487846), and this PR follows it. The server pins sit in the existing `runtime-config-upgrade-url.test.ts` harness, and the reader pins sit in the shared `runtime-config.test.ts`. The page pin is a new card-named file, because no shared harness exists for that link.
  - (2) The trailing signed comment. It is the relay's sanctioned PR-body signature form, `PR_BODY_TRAILER_SHAPE` in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`, which the relay reads with `readSignatureLine`. PR-body guards are green, so option A stands.
- **Security.** No refused scheme reaches the payload (see ①). The console takes the served value verbatim, with no second scheme check. It inherits the producer's refusal from the runtime's own same-origin endpoint, so no user-controlled input reaches the `href`, and there is no open-redirect path in the console.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** Not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. It reads one host option and one served field. No finding.
- **Nits** (none affects correctness or the contract; all may stay open):
  - N1. The console reader trusts the producer's http(s) refusal and does not re-check the scheme. This is parity with the `upgradeUrl` reader, as the claim states. A console-side check would be defence in depth for both keys together, not for this slice alone.
  - N2. The PR body's Tests section says "five refused values (relative, bare host, `javascript:`, `ftp:`)". That names four categories for five values, because two of the values are relative spellings. It is cosmetic only.
  - N3. The seat's design confirmation ("Design confirmed by the seat before code") is stated in the restated claim 6953457788 and not in a seat comment of its own on the card. The ruling holds on its merits (see ①, the runtime-only ruling).

No must-fix or should-fix finding.
